claim_map.title: Regional business scope
claim_map.text:
The Indonesia proposal places local back-office data onshore while retaining the same portal and GBS KL processing.
Indonesia users access Indonesia data. Other local-country users require approval for Indonesia access.
The documented proposal also permits group users. CES regional scope and the GDC performance benchmark remain design requirements.
The source proposes no new profiles or business functionality and expects reporting continuity.

claim_map.title: Later isolation and provisioning choice
claim_map.text:
The later solutioning requires isolation of related data, including rules and static data.
Earlier assumptions, alternatives A/B/C, and discarded shared-data sections remain historical alternatives.
The selected provisioning diagram 3 uses the GDC Murex adaptor to convert real-time and batch input into SCBML.
Message Bridge routes Indonesia events through FM Solace. Non-Indonesia events retain their existing path.
The source also mentions GDC adaptor database persistence. Its compatibility with the isolation requirement remains unresolved.
Direct downstream access to Indonesia APIs is a preference, without recorded final approval.

claim_map.title: Fixing-flag delivery without cross-country NAS
claim_map.text:
Indonesia cannot use cross-country NAS for the fixing batch.
The proposed GDC batch processing queries the adaptor for the booking entity and publishes Indonesia events to Kafka.
Message Bridge transports those events through FM Solace into Indonesia Kafka.
Indonesia consumes those events and follows the intended fixing-revert process.
The adaptor supplies the cashflow and booking-entity FMID lookup interface.

claim_map.title: Integration and identifier boundaries
claim_map.text:
The integration plan names `Cash_Settlement_Mxg_Inbound_Batch_All` for GDC batch publication to Message Bridge.
It requires separate netting and splitting resultant-ID prefixes. Folder-route retention remains a question.

claim_map.title: API routing and regional identifiers
claim_map.text:
The design proposes an `/idns/` API prefix and importmap overrides for regional routing.
SSO, authentication, and public resources remain on the GDC path without that prefix.
It proposes configurable distinct netting and splitting prefixes. Contradictory SID/NID examples cannot establish a final identifier format.
The onboarding table includes an Indonesia LMS blacklist. Separate sender-filter-removal proposals require scoped reconciliation.
Historical SSI whitelist text includes literal `LOANID`; this review does not normalize that label or establish current membership.

claim_map.title: Custom-view API relocation
claim_map.text:
The migration table assigns `/v2/customview/filters` and `/v2/customview/views` to the Indonesia cash-settlement query service.
The source describes an intended API relocation, without completed implementation or compatibility evidence.

claim_map.title: Regional drawer filtering proposal
claim_map.text:
The drawer design adds `entry_name` and JSON `filter_rule` to tile and audit configuration.
The Indonesia expression checks FMID `8`; the GDC expression checks whether any FMID differs from `8`.
The example uses application `51358` and `RATAN_ENTITLEMENT_RULE`. These are source-scoped configuration descriptions.
The failure table hides drawers when EMS3 is unavailable or the filter is empty.
The same table says to show a drawer when its rule mismatches. That unresolved fail-open case prevents a complete accepted failure contract.
The proposed Redis cache lifetime is 3600 seconds. It supplies no cache execution evidence.
Historical EMS2/EMS3 responsibilities do not override later explicit CES migration intent.

claim_map.title: Regional tile presentation
claim_map.text:
The tile proposal groups settlement, business-rule, and static functions to reduce duplicate tile presentation.
Administrative fields include title, subtitle, regional filter rule, and entry name.
The documented Global and Indonesia examples use separate FMID expressions.
Unselected user rows and linked screenshots cannot establish the complete visibility matrix.

claim_map.title: Regional UI behavior
claim_map.text:
The intended regional deployment keeps GDC and Indonesia tiles independent.
Trade cashflow-detail navigation selects the region from the booking entity.
Indonesia blotter entity dropdowns include Indonesia only.
Indonesia dashboard cards open Indonesia cashflow or grouping blotters.
The scope also includes global-rule synchronization from GDC.

claim_map.title: UI integration scope
claim_map.text:
The UI scope repeats regional entity filtering, dashboard navigation, trade-detail routing, and global-rule synchronization.
It also names Indonesia timezone support, portal tiles, and regional view/filter APIs.
A source-reported residual GDC URL issue remains task evidence, not an intended routing rule.

claim_map.title: UAT reporting and data entitlement intent
claim_map.text:
The UAT scope requires SSDR reporting through DQSL and retains manual settlement touchpoints.
Only users with FMCES and Indonesia access may view the scoped data.
This is a UAT-scope requirement, not a passing UAT or current entitlement finding.

claim_map.title: Infrastructure handover requirements
claim_map.text:
The handover checklist requires application-ready VMs, PostgreSQL, network/firewall access, ITRS configuration, and support permissions with sign-off.
Dependencies include OLA/SLA, DR testing, ADO pipeline integration, database initialization, and Global-to-Indonesia Message Bridge integration.
The checklist defines expected handover inputs; it does not establish completed provisioning.

claim_map.title: Planned cutover safeguards
claim_map.text:
The selected release-plan row proposes upstream/downstream switching, migration job holds, and GDC CPT control for Indonesia.
It proposes suppressing migrated READY cashflows in GDC to avoid duplicate payments.
The row also proposes truncating existing cashflows. This historical plan grants no execution or deletion authorization.
Its literal `05-Dec` date has no established year in the selected content.
